question: Which of the following wars took place in the year 1761?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Panipat III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on **January 14, 1761**, between the Maratha Empire and the Durrani Empire (Afghan forces led by Ahmad Shah Abdali).
 
• This battle is considered one of the largest and bloodiest fought in the 18th century, involving over 125,000 soldiers.
 
• The Marathas were led by their commander-in-chief, **Sadashivrao Bhau**, while the Afghan forces were commanded by Ahmad Shah Abdali.
 
• The battle resulted in a decisive victory for the Durrani Empire, marking the end of Maratha expansion in North India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Causes of the Battle:**

 
 
• The Marathas aimed to expand their influence in Northern India, which led to conflicts with regional powers including the Durrani Empire.
 
• The battle was also a result of the declining Mughal Empire, which left a power vacuum in the region.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures:**
 
 
• Ahmad Shah Abdali, also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani, was the founder of the Durrani Empire and one of the most successful military leaders of his time.
 
• Sadashivrao Bhau, the Maratha commander-in-chief, was the nephew of the Peshwa and a capable military leader.
 
 
 
• **Consequences:**
 
 
• The defeat at Panipat weakened the Maratha Empire significantly, leading to internal strife and a temporary setback in their quest for dominance.
 
• The battle also paved the way for the eventual rise of British power in India as the Marathas were one of the main obstacles to their expansion.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat is remembered for its high casualties and the significant impact it had on the Indian subcontinent's political landscape.
 
• It is often studied as a key example of the complex interplay of regional powers during the 18th century in India.
